easy.def: To leave a place because of danger.
examples: We evacuated the building.
The people evacuated the town.
Everyone evacuated.

more.def: To leave a place quickly because it is not safe.
examples: The school evacuated when the fire alarm rang.
The town was evacuated before the flood.
Everyone evacuated the building calmly.

easy.def: Leaving a place quickly because of danger.
examples: The fire drill is an evacuation.
The evacuation was calm.
The town had an evacuation.

more.def: The act of moving people out of a place quickly because it is not safe.
examples: During the fire drill, the evacuation of the school took four minutes.
The town ordered an evacuation before the storm hit.
The evacuation was calm, and everyone got out safely.

easy.def: To get away from something by being clever.
examples: The rabbit evaded the fox.
She evaded the question.
He evaded the ball.

more.def: To avoid or escape from someone or something, often by being clever.
examples: The rabbit evaded the fox by darting into a hole.
She evaded the question with a smile.
The fish evaded the net.

related.def: The act of judging how good something is.

easy.def: To think about how good something is.
examples: The teacher will evaluate my work.
We evaluate the plan.
Let's evaluate the results.

more.def: To think carefully about something to decide how good, useful or important it is.
examples: The judges evaluated each science project before choosing a winner.
The teacher evaluated our stories and gave us tips.
We evaluated the results of the experiment to see if the plant grew faster.

easy.def: To turn from water into a gas in the air.
examples: The puddle will evaporate in the sun.
Water evaporates when it is hot.
The water evaporated from the dish.

more.def: To change from a liquid into a gas, such as water turning into vapor and rising into the air.
examples: Puddles evaporate when the sun comes out.
The sun makes ocean water evaporate and rise into the sky.
We watched the water evaporate from the pan on the stove.

easy.def: The night or day before a special day.
examples: We went to bed on Christmas Eve.
It is the eve of my birthday.
On the eve of the trip, I packed.

more.def: The evening or day just before a holiday or an important event.
examples: On the eve of the big game, the team had a quiet dinner.
Children often feel excited on the eve of a holiday.
We packed our bags on the eve of the trip.

easy.def: Used to show something is surprising.
examples: Even the baby laughed.
It is even bigger than me.
She did not even cry.

more.def: Used to stress that something is more than you might think.
examples: Even the tallest kid could not reach the top shelf.
The day was cold, and it was even colder at night.
He was so tired that he could not even stand.

easy.def: Flat and smooth.
examples: The floor is even.
An even road is easy to ride on.
The table is not even.

more.def: Flat and level, or the same in amount or size.
examples: The path across the field was smooth and even.
The two teams were even at halftime, with five points each.
Cut the cake into even pieces so everyone gets the same.

easy.def: The time at the end of the day.
examples: We eat dinner in the evening.
It is cool in the evening.
Good evening, everyone!

more.def: The part of the day between afternoon and night.
examples: In the evening, the owls start to hoot.
We watched the sunset on a warm summer evening.
My family takes a walk every evening.

easy.def: In a way that is equal or smooth.
examples: Spread the jam evenly.
Share the cake evenly.
The paint was spread evenly.

more.def: In an equal or smooth way, with no part more than another.
examples: Spread the butter evenly over the bread.
The teacher divided the paper evenly among the students.
The paint was applied evenly across the wall.

easy.def: Numbers like 2, 4 and 6.
examples: Two, four and six are evens.
Count by evens.
Add the evens.

more.def: Numbers that can be divided exactly by two, like 2, 4 and 6.
examples: All the numbers on the left side of the street are evens.
We counted by evens.
Add up all the evens on the list.

easy.def: Something that happens.
examples: The party was a fun event.
The big event is today.
The picnic is a school event.

more.def: Something that happens, especially something important or planned.
examples: The school fair is the biggest event of the year.
A storm was the main event of the week.
The swimming event starts at noon.

easy.def: Coming later in the end.
examples: The eventual winner.
The eventual result.
The eventual end was happy.

more.def: Happening at last, after other things have happened.
examples: The eventual winner crossed the line last year.
The eventual result of the study was clear.
The eventual end of the story was happy.

easy.def: After a long time.
examples: Eventually, the rain stopped.
The seed will eventually grow.
He eventually fell asleep.

more.def: At last, after a long time or many steps.
examples: Eventually, the snow melted and the grass grew.
After many tries, she eventually learned to ride the bike.
The bus was late, but it eventually arrived.

easy.def: At any time.
examples: Have you ever swum?
Did you ever see a whale?
It is the best cake ever.

more.def: At any time, or at all times.
examples: Have you ever seen a shooting star?
This was the biggest fish he had ever caught.
The tree has been growing ever since I was a baby.

easy.def: A tree that stays green all year.
examples: A pine is an evergreen.
The evergreen is green.
We decorate an evergreen.

more.def: A tree or bush that has green leaves all year round.
examples: A pine is an evergreen that keeps its needles in winter.
Evergreens stay green when other trees lose their leaves.
We hung lights on the evergreen by the door.

easy.def: Lasting forever.
examples: They promised everlasting friendship.
An everlasting love.
The story has an everlasting ending.

more.def: Lasting forever, or for such a long time that it never seems to end.
examples: The two friends promised each other an everlasting friendship.
The explorer dreamed of everlasting fame.
The old tale says that the lamp gives an everlasting light.

easy.def: Each one of a group.
examples: I brush my teeth every day.
Every kid got a prize.
She knows every word.

more.def: Each one of a group, with none left out, or each time something happens.
examples: Every student in the class got a turn on the swing.
We visit my grandmother every Sunday.
He cleaned every corner of the room.

easy.def: All the people.
examples: Everybody is here.
Everybody sang.
Hello, everybody!

more.def: Every person in a group.
examples: Everybody in the class got a turn on the swing.
The teacher asked everybody to line up at the door.
Everybody cheered when the team scored.

easy.def: Ordinary and used every day.
examples: I wear everyday clothes.
This is an everyday plate.
It is an everyday job.

more.def: Ordinary and used or seen on any normal day.
examples: I wear everyday shoes to school.
Cooking is an everyday task.
The everyday dishes are in the cupboard.

easy.def: All the people.
examples: Everyone is here.
Hello, everyone!
Everyone clapped.

more.def: Every person in a group.
examples: Everyone in the class brought a snack to share.
The teacher waited until everyone was quiet.
Everyone cheered when the team won.

easy.def: All the things.
examples: I packed everything.
Everything is ready.
She knows everything.

more.def: All things, or each thing in a group.
examples: We packed everything into the car before the trip.
Everything in the room was covered with dust.
The kitten wants to explore everything.

easy.def: In every place.
examples: Toys are everywhere.
I looked everywhere.
Leaves were everywhere.

more.def: In or to every place.
examples: Snow covered everything everywhere.
I searched everywhere for my hat.
Bees were buzzing everywhere in the garden.

easy.def: To make someone leave the place where they live.
examples: The owner evicted the family.
They were evicted.
He evicted the people.

more.def: To make someone leave the home they live in, usually because they have not paid or have broken a rule.
examples: The landlord evicted the tenants when they did not pay the rent.
The family was evicted from their old apartment.
The bird evicted the squirrel from the nest.

easy.def: Facts that show something is true.
examples: Footprints are evidence that a deer came by.
The clues were evidence.
We found evidence of a fox.

more.def: Facts or signs that show that something is true.
examples: Muddy footprints were evidence that someone had come in.
Scientists look for evidence before they decide.
The nibbled leaves were evidence of a rabbit.

easy.def: Easy to see or to know.
examples: It is evident that she is happy.
The answer was evident.
His joy was evident.

more.def: Easy to see or understand, because it is very clear.
examples: It was evident from the muddy shoes that the dog had been in the garden.
Her excitement was evident from the huge smile on her face.
The dark clouds made it evident that rain was coming.

easy.def: As anyone can easily see.
examples: It is evidently raining.
He evidently likes cake.
She is evidently happy.

more.def: In a way that is clear to see from the facts.
examples: The little boy was evidently tired, because he fell asleep on the bus.
It had evidently rained, because the sidewalk was wet.
She was evidently excited about the trip and talked about it all day.

easy.def: Very bad and cruel.
examples: The evil witch cast a spell.
The evil king was mean.
It was an evil plan.

more.def: Very bad and cruel, and wishing to hurt others.
examples: The evil queen in the fairy tale was cruel to everyone.
The hero stopped the evil plan.
In the story, an evil wizard cast a spell.

easy.def: Slow change over a long time.
examples: The evolution of animals took long.
The evolution of the bike.
Evolution is slow.

more.def: The slow change of living things over millions of years, or any slow development.
examples: The evolution of birds took millions of years.
The evolution of the telephone is interesting.
Scientists study evolution.

easy.def: About how living things change slowly over a long time.
examples: There is an evolutionary link.
The evolutionary change took a long time.
An evolutionary story is told here.

more.def: Having to do with evolution, the slow change of living things over many, many years.
examples: Scientists study the evolutionary history of birds.
Long necks were an evolutionary change in giraffes.
The museum showed an evolutionary chart of horses.

easy.def: To change slowly over a long time.
examples: Animals evolve.
The plant evolved.
The story evolved.

more.def: To change and develop slowly over a very long time.
examples: Animals evolve over millions of years.
The game evolved as people added new rules.
The small town evolved into a big city.
